questions: The plausible alternatives are shared negation requiring both absences; independently negated alternatives requiring either absence; narrow negation leaving a profit objective affirmative; and a contextual reading retaining an independent business-operation inquiry. Does the irregular coordination reflect shared negation or a drafting error? Context favors shared negation but does not settle the wording.

Should independently negated alternatives be retained as an editorial reconstruction? Its expression is (and genuine_family_arrangement (or (not income_beyond_reimbursement) (not profit_objective))). TRUE would require genuineness and either absence, supplying an omitted negative auxiliary while preserving disjunction.

Can narrow negation survive the surrounding treatment of profit purpose? Its expression is (and genuine_family_arrangement (or (not income_beyond_reimbursement) profit_objective)). TRUE would require genuineness and either no additional income or an affirmative profit objective. This is syntactically arguable but contextually strained.

Can the referenced Circular or a verified source version clarify the coordination and parenthetical? The missing dependency and any parallel-language text have not been supplied; critic agreement and duplicate formulas cannot resolve their meaning.
Can the selected_slice metadata be aligned with issue.question? The retained readings answer only antecedent satisfaction, not the broader licensing trigger.

Does the sentence identify a sufficient, defeasible category without exhausting other grounds for non-business status? Neither FALSE nor failure to establish TRUE supports the converse licensing conclusion.
No exclusive-disjunction reading is retained: what textual basis, if any, would justify excluding an arrangement satisfying both negative conditions?

citations.quote: A genuine single family office arrangement, established to serve the investment needs of members of a single family, which is not being run as a business (i.e. not receiving any income, other than reimbursement of operating expenses from the family) or have the pursuit of profit as its business objective, should not in the ordinary course be considered as carrying on a business from a licensing perspective.
the activity is capable of making profit; and the activity was carried out for the purpose of making profit.
It is also not the SFC’s intent to extend its regulatory oversight to this type of single family office setup.

readings.distinction: After considering the alternatives listed in questions, shared negation is contextually preferred: profit purpose is a business-status consideration, and the following regulatory-intent sentence supports a non-commercial category. TRUE means genuineness and both absences. The formula is equivalent to negating the disjunction of income and profit objective; that equivalent expression is not another reading. The defective verb coordination prevents treating this preference as conclusive.

readings.distinction: TRUE would require a genuine arrangement, the income restriction, no profit objective, and non-business operation assessed on the relevant circumstances. Identical supplied Boolean values need not settle that additional inquiry. The preceding paragraph supports this contextual possibility, but does not expressly add an antecedent condition; “i.e.” weighs against it. It remains an unresolved alternative, not an established extra requirement.

vocabulary_concerns: The income fact means any income other than reimbursement of operating expenses from the family; it does not mean net profit or receipts exceeding expenses. Attribution of receipts to the office rather than family investments, and classification of reimbursements, remain judgment-dependent.

Profit objective, profit capability, realized income and continuity are distinct. The supplied facts do not distinguish the office's commercial objective from the family's investment objectives without interpretive judgment.

The fixed vocabulary cannot independently express case-specific business operation or how the listed factors combine. The income abstraction is local and cannot establish a general definition of carrying on a business in Hong Kong.

Genuine family arrangement requires judgment. Q1 supplies no statutory definition of family or family office; Q2's typical arrangement and often-used corporate structure do not establish mandatory structural requirements.

The Boolean records antecedent satisfaction only. It does not encode qualified ordinary-course guidance, regulatory intent, exceptions, regulated activities, carve-outs or territory. TRUE establishes no exemption, and FALSE establishes no licensing obligation.
The same-period and unknown-evidence conventions are modeling assumptions. The source supplies no precise accounting period or timing rule.
The mismatch in the coordinated verbs is textual uncertainty, not an unknown factual input. The expression language can represent competing attachments, but cannot determine which the source intends.
